correctness.rationale: The degree-(s+1) plane model is smooth and has genus s(s-1)/2. A checked shift delta^s+delta=-eta gives a nonzero trace-zero Frobenius cocycle b=eta-eta^s. The Hermitian H has s^3+1 points, forcing all 2g eigenvalues -s. Its order-s translation quotient is P1, giving zero invariant H1; norm-scaling automorphisms permute the s-1 nontrivial U-characters transitively, each multiplicity s. Thus twist eigenvalues -s*psi(a) yield the product and, by additive orthogonality, all extension counts. The exact finite checker (12 cases including p=2 and r=2) agrees; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Compared full statements, not titles alone. Homma--Kim first classify the N_q=1 curve, but their displayed assertions do not provide the all-extension Hasse--Weil characteristic polynomial. A related 2015 Artin--Schreier zeta theorem concerns untwisted forms and does not imply the nonzero Hermitian translation cocycle spectrum. The explicit new representation-theoretic multiplicity yields an independent, uniform conclusion for every square field. Relevant search hits were checked for mathematical implication; no covering result was identified, with an inaccessible same-author chapter recorded as a residual risk.
residual_risks: The full Springer 2026 chapter on projective equivalence was not accessible; its abstract does not establish absence of an implicit Frobenius statement.
A general theorem or tabulation of unipotent Hermitian twists may imply the polynomial without using the newer Hermitian-relative terminology.
Semantic search and selected primary reading cannot establish global uniqueness or an independent mathematical certification.

value.rationale: The 2026 classification discovers a naturally extremal one-rational-point Hermitian-relative class and gives no extension arithmetic. The uniform L-polynomial determines its entire F_{q^n} point sequence, its p-periodic deviation and the precise Hermitian descent over F_{q^p} across all prime powers. This is a motivated, complete arithmetic invariant for a geometrically natural family; no paper-sized or unrelated downstream theorem is required.
